outcome: The Brumer–Stark conjecture (the case of the Stark conjectures this bullet names) was proved by Dasgupta–Kakde in 2020 (away from p=2) and extended to a full proof over Z by Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang in October 2023 — both before the frozen revision. The general (non-abelian, higher-rank) Stark conjectures remain open. Post-window activity found is confined to a distinct, related question: explicit p-adic formulas for the already-proven-to-exist Brumer–Stark units (Honnor 2023/2024/2025; Dasgupta–Honnor–Spieß 2022/2025), which is a refinement/constructive-formula question tied to Hilbert's 12th problem, not a further resolution of the existence conjecture itself.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet names 'Stark conjectures (including Brumer–Stark conjecture)'. The Brumer–Stark conjecture — that certain Brumer–Stark units exist with p-order equal to a partial zeta value — was proved away from p=2 by Dasgupta and Kakde (arXiv:2010.00657, submitted 2020-10-01, published in Annals of Mathematics 2023) and extended to a full unconditional proof over Z by Dasgupta, Kakde, Silliman and Wang (arXiv:2310.16399, submitted 2023-10-26). Both events predate the frozen revision (2024-01-26), so this case of the general Stark conjectures is correctly status open_stale, dated to the October 2023 full proof (the later, more complete event, per §6.1). The broader Stark conjectures (arbitrary rank, non-abelian settings) remain open; I found no post-window result settling any further case of those. What I did find post-window is a cluster of papers on a related but distinct question: explicit formulas expressing the (already known to exist) Brumer–Stark units p-adically. Matthew Honnor's paper (arXiv:2302.12332) had v1 in Feb 2023 (pre-window) but v2, posted 2024-01-11, proved a strictly stronger result resolving an additional root-of-unity ambiguity at p=2 and removing an assumption from Dasgupta–Kakde's formula — this is a genuine post-window strengthening, but it targets the Dasgupta–Kakde explicit-formula conjecture, not the Brumer–Stark existence conjecture itself. A companion paper, Dasgupta–Honnor–Spieß 'On the Equality of Three Formulas for Brumer–Stark Units' (arXiv:2211.01715, v1 Nov 2022, substantially revised Dec 2025, published in J. London Math. Soc. Oct 2025) proves three conjectural p-adic formulas for the units agree; this too is about the explicit-formula/Hilbert's-12th-problem side of the theory, not the existence conjecture. Neither paper's abstract or introduction (as accessible) frames the formula question as a literal restatement of the Brumer–Stark conjecture as Wikipedia states it; the existence question was already closed before the window, and the formula question is a related, Hilbert-12-flavored refinement that a careful reading of the bullet would not fold into 'the Stark conjectures' entry as newly resolved or newly partial. No AI system was found anywhere in this cluster of work — all papers are traditional human-authored algebraic number theory (Iwasawa theory, Hilbert modular forms, Ritter–Weiss modules, Eisenstein congruences); searches for AI/ML involvement in Stark or Brumer–Stark work returned nothing relevant.
competing_reading: One could argue the Dasgupta–Spieß explicit-formula conjecture is close enough to 'the Brumer–Stark conjecture' in spirit (both are about pinning down these units completely and both trace to the same research program aimed at Hilbert's 12th problem) that Honnor's Jan 2024 strengthening and the Dec 2025 equality-of-three-formulas result should count as `partial`/`progress` post-window movement on this bullet, with event date 2024-01-11 (Honnor v2) rather than open_stale. Under that reading ai_role would still be none.
what_would_settle_it: A careful reading of Tate's original Brumer–Stark conjecture statement and the Dasgupta–Kakde papers' own framing of whether the explicit p-adic formula is presented as part of the conjecture's statement or as a separate conjecture (sometimes called the Dasgupta–Spieß conjecture) built on top of it; if the latter, as the papers' own titles and structure suggest, open_stale is correct.
